text: Proposition forty-one combines audits with changes to state
spending-limit rules.
The measure concerns new or increased state special
taxes.
The initial audit must identify ways to reduce
annual program costs by ten percent.
Identifying options is not the same as delivering
savings or proving that services can stay unchanged.
Prop forty-one could block Prop forty if both
pass and forty-one receives more yes votes, subject
to how courts interpret their conflict.
A voter might want evidence of efficiency before
approving new dedicated taxes, and regular follow-up
afterward.
Another voter could favor oversight but object to
mandatory reviews of measures that never qualify, or
to limits on funding flexibility.
Yes adds audits and spending-limit provisions;
no keeps the current framework.
